key_insight: METTA combines fine-grained neural memory with compact episode summaries to adapt to unseen tasks without attending over the full interaction history.
engineering_relevance: Its two-timescale memory design offers a path to scalable long-context meta-RL with linear sequence complexity for within-episode adaptation.
method: Use causal neural memory for fine-grained within-episode adaptation.
Retain compact episode summaries for cross-episode task inference.
Enable test-time training to adapt to held-out tasks and task families.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports over 50% success on held-out Meta-World ML10/45 test environments and better performance than transformer baselines on long-context, sparse-reward PointMaze tasks.
watch_item: Compact episode summaries may omit useful task evidence; the abstract does not quantify this trade-off or specify exact compute budgets.
paper_title: METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning
